messages.author: 3033a60610caec0b
messages.subject: Problems with ggsave(type = "pdf") on Mac
parts:
This issue deals with ggsave. When using ggsave (type = "pdf") on a
Mac (see sessionInfo below), linetype = 5, or at least the fifth
linetype that ggplot chooses, gets lost in the save. The plot displays
properly onscreen in an R session, but does not display properly in
the pdf.

For an example of the pdf, see "ggsave_linetype_bug.pdf" in Files.

Thanks,
Brandon

<CODE>


# Code to illustrate missing line type 5 in legend
ctry <- rep(c("US","UK", "EU", "JP", "BR"), each = 5)
x <- (runif(25) - 1 * 5)
y <- (runif(25) - 1 * 5)

plotData <- data.frame(ctry, x, y, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sapply(plotData, class)


p1 <- qplot(x, y, data = plotData, geom="line", linetype = ctry)
ggsave(filename = "test.pdf", plot = p1)

# > sessionInfo()
# R version 2.8.1 (2008-12-22)
# i386-apple-darwin8.11.1
#
# locale:
# en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8
#
# attached base packages:
# [1] grid stats graphics grDevices utils datasets
# [7] methods base
#
# other attached packages:
# [1] ggplot2_0.8.2 reshape_0.8.2 plyr_0.1.4 proto_0.3-8

messages.subject: Re: Problems with ggsave(type = "pdf") on Mac
parts:
Hadley,

It does appear that the problem has to do with "on stretches" of
linetypes of length = 1. They are all lost in the pdf processing on
the Mac. I have reviewed the documentation and have figured out how to
define a manual scale. However, I can't figure out how to get just a
solid line, in addition to the dot-dash lines. See below.

# This works
linetypes <- c("82", "21", "42", "44", "4424", "6363")

p1 + scale_linetype_manual(values = linetypes)

# However, the following linetypes definitions don't work
linetypes <- c(NULL, "11", "31", "33", "3313", "4242")
linetypes <- c(NA, "11", "31", "33", "3313", "4242")
linetypes <- c("00", "11", "31", "33", "3313", "4242")

p1 + scale_linetype_manual(values = linetypes)
